items.stem: Which of the following statements about the fundamental principle of counting is correct?
items.answer: If one event can occur in m ways and, after it, another in n ways, both can occur in m × n ways.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: "If one event can occur in m ways and, after it, another in n ways, both can occur in m × n ways." The other three are false.
options: If one event can occur in m ways and, after it, another in n ways, both can occur in m × n ways.
Rolling two dice gives 6 + 6 = 12 outcomes.
The number of 2-digit numbers with distinct digits is 10 × 9 = 90.
If one event can occur in m ways and another in n ways, both can occur in m + n ways.

items.stem: State the fundamental principle of counting and illustrate it with an example.
items.answer: If an event can occur in m ways and, following it, another in n ways, together they occur in mn ways; e.g. 3 shirts and 2 trousers give 6 outfits.
items.markingKey: 1 + 1 marks.
